text:
Dan: hey all, dan here — first day on runtime team. trying to build from source on ubuntu 24.04, cuda 11.8, gcc 12. getting a ptxas/ptx error during link, halp
Dan: error snippet:
```
ptxas fatal : ValueError: unsupported PTX version '8.7'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
Dan: build command is `make -j8 BUILD_USE_CUDA=1` from main branch
Mika: welcome! short checklist: check `nvcc --version`, `nvidia-smi`, and ensure CUDA_HOME points to /usr/local/cuda-11.8
Mika: also what driver version do you have? cuda 11.8 usually wants >= 525.x drivers
Dan: nvcc says Cuda compilation tools, release 11.8, V11.8.89
Dan: nvidia-smi shows Driver Version: 520.61.05
Natanael: ah, 520 may be borderline. ptxas complaining about PTX version often means the driver/toolkit disagree on supported PTX arch. try upgrading driver to 525+ if you can
Evan: alternatively, set CUDAHOSTCXX to g++-11 if you have mismatched gcc. but ptxas text looks driver/toolkit mismatch more than gcc
Dan: we can't bump drivers on this workstation (corp laptop). any workaround?
Rosie: you can build with a lower compute capability target as a stopgap: set `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="6.0;7.0;7.5"` or whatever your GPU supports. that will avoid generating newer PTX.
Mika: also check which ptxas binary is being used: `which ptxas` and `ptxas --version` — sometimes leftover `/usr/local/cuda/bin` vs packaged tools conflict
Dan: `which ptxas` -> /usr/local/cuda-11.8/bin/ptxas
Dan: `ptxas --version` -> 10.6.0 -> ???
Natanael: that ptxas from toolkit might still generate PTX v8.7 if the backend compiler is newer. if you can't upgrade drivers, try building with `-arch=sm_70` flags or set env `CUDA_NVCC_FLAGS="-gencode arch=compute_70,code=sm_70"`
Evan: note: for reproducible onboarding, we maintain a dev container image in infra: `redwood/runtime-dev:cuda11.8-gcc12-ubi` — if you can use that via `docker run --privileged -v /tmp/.X11-unix:/tmp/.X11-unix ...` it avoids laptop driver issues for build (but not for runtime)
infra-bot: CI image for runtime builds: registry.redwood/internal/runtime-dev:cuda11.8-gcc12-2026-02-15
Dan: i'm on corp laptop so docker with privileged GPU passthrough needs infra approval, will try local hacks first
Rosie: quick try: add `--ptxas-options=-v` to see what it's compiling and confirm arch target. also grep for `-gencode` in build logs to see if newer arch is injected
Dan: ran make with `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` set to sm_70 and build proceeded past ptxas stage, now hitting a different link error but progress :)
Mika: nice! if you can paste new linker error we can help — sometimes you need to symlink `libcudart.so` into /usr/lib or add `-L/usr/local/cuda/lib64` to LDFLAGS
Dan: new error is `undefined reference to cublasLtCreate` during runtime linking
Evan: that one usually means link order or missing `-lcublasLt`. ensure `-lcublasLt -lcublas -lcudart` sequence. also check `/usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64/libcublasLt.so` exists
Dan: libcublasLt.so is present, adding link order fix in Makefile fixed it. build finished! :tada:
Dan: thanks all — will file a short onboarding note with: driver min version, TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST tip, and cublaslt link order gotcha
Mika: perfect, ping me and i'll add it to the eng-runtime onboarding doc
Rosie: welcome aboard Dan :wave:
Dan: thanks! I'll add the doc and the commands I ran to a gist and share here
